_comment: Upstream digests for the committed .fabro fork. Regenerate with `just refresh-fork-upstream-pins`; every entry MUST carry a reason. See crates/console-fork-drift-check/src/lib.rs.

files.reason: ABSENT FROM OUR FORK BY CONSTRUCTION. Upstream added a whole `disposition` stage; our workflow.fabro has zero references to it. Adopting it is a graph change, not a file copy. `present_in_fork: false` records that this omission is known, so the gate does not report it as a missing file every run.
DIVERGED only slightly from upstream. Low-risk to sync; not yet reviewed.

DIVERGED. Upstream has grown honest-checks / no-detector-evasion, cohesion-decomposition and verbatim-move rules we have not adopted. Porting them is wanted but is its own reviewed change, not a silent sync.

SYNCED VERBATIM from upstream 2026-07-28 (PR #476, merged 2026-07-28T22:08:32Z) — our copy had been frozen at 3fa2d5c and lacked the fetch+rebase publish leg that upstream landed as bd-ib-qq7f (PR #905). Keep it verbatim: a local 'improvement' to borrowed prose becomes a divergence nobody remembers agreeing to. The retry's exact-match ci.yml scoping is a known upstream wart, filed with factory-hardening; we inherit the fix when they ship it.

DELIBERATELY NOT SYNCED, same reason as review.md — and upstream has additionally rewritten it to consume a `disposition` record that our graph does not produce, so syncing it alone would reference a stage we do not run.

DELIBERATELY NOT SYNCED. This repo's review gate is ADVISORY / ship-on-cap by recorded decision (workflow.fabro, work-item bd-ib-egms32); upstream's is BLOCKING by default. Syncing would silently revert a ratified policy. Re-pin on upstream change only after confirming the change is policy-neutral.

DIVERGED. Our graph encodes the advisory ship-on-cap review gate (see :9-10, bd-ib-egms32) and omits upstream's disposition stage. This is the file the fork exists to own; treat any upstream movement here as a design review, never a sync.

DIVERGED, AND THIS IS THE REASON THE FORK EXISTS: our docker pin is the `python-rust-agent-` sandbox layer, while upstream pins `python-agent-`, which its own comment documents as carrying no Rust. This is a Rust repo, so inheriting upstream's image would fail every cargo build. Note our copy is rewritten continuously by the pin-bump automation; that never affects this gate, which pins UPSTREAM's bytes, not ours. Upstream also carries github permissions, a different review adapter, disposition_adapter, review_fix_visit_cap and step-timer wrapping that we have not evaluated. REVIEWED 2026-07-29 (first live firing of this gate, ~hours after it landed): upstream moved ff41a734 -> 74df8da9, and the whole diff is ONE line — its docker pin going python-agent-v0.57.0 -> v1.0.3. Nothing to port: that is upstream's own layer prefix on its own bump cadence, and our copy tracks OUR dev-tooling pin independently (both at v1.0.0 as of 4080e3c). Re-pinned deliberately, not refreshed-to-green. Note pr.md did NOT move, so the retry-signature fix has not shipped yet. REVIEWED 2026-07-30 (second live firing; upstream 74df8da9 -> 9528c0df, plugin 856d699b5f7d -> 1fc573da09c5, bumped by this session's own SessionStart hook). The diff is TWO hunks and they were dispositioned SEPARATELY. (1) docker pin python-agent-v1.0.3 -> v1.8.0: NOT PORTED, same standing reason as above — that is upstream's own no-Rust layer prefix on its own cadence. (2) NEW `commit_timeout = "10m"`: PORTED VERBATIM into our fork in this same change, which is why this pin moves with a code change rather than alone. Upstream added it because Fabro's stock 30s checkpoint budget destroyed completed work in gate-heavy repos (their ledger bd-ib-6ka), and we are that case: our fork carried NO commit_timeout, `skip_git_hooks = false` means checkpoint commits run our hooks, and those hooks measured 91.76s (pre-commit) and 251-273s (pre-push check) on this host the same day. Counter-evidence recorded so the risk is not overstated: five dispatches succeeded here on 2026-07-29 without the fix, so the hazard is real but not certain to fire. Re-pinned deliberately, not refreshed-to-green. pr.md STILL has not moved, so the retry-signature fix remains unshipped upstream. REVIEWED 2026-07-30 (third live firing; plugin cache advanced to 0.49.2 during this run): upstream's new delta adds GitHub permission/token-refresh wiring, switches the review adapter to the current package name, and carries disposition-stage defaults. NOT PORTED here because this PR is the console AGENTS.md gh-checks guidance change, while those upstream hunks alter dispatch credentials, model adapter selection, or graph stages this fork intentionally omits. Our fork already carries the load-bearing checkpoint timeout and keeps the Rust agent image pin. Re-pinned deliberately so this unrelated publish-stage drift does not block the gh guidance fix. REVIEWED 2026-07-30 (FOURTH firing, and the FIRST whose cause is NOT upstream moving). No upstream change is being dispositioned here. The previous entry re-pinned to b6e3ebe7cb4a against a plugin cache resolved as `0.49.2`; on this host the drift check resolves the INSTALLED plugin as 1fc573da09c5, whose workflow.toml is 9528c0dfa1a7 — the value already reviewed and dispositioned in the entry before it. So the gate went red not because our fork drifted but because two sessions resolved DIFFERENT installed plugin versions and each re-pinned against its own. Nothing to port: the bytes at 9528c0dfa1a7 are the ones whose two hunks were dispositioned above (docker pin declined, commit_timeout ported). STRUCTURAL NOTE for whoever touches this next, because a re-pin here is NOT idempotent across hosts: this fixture pins a digest, but the digest it must match depends on which plugin build the LOCAL machine resolves. While `installed_plugins.json` can resolve mixed versions (see livespec-console-beads-fabro-pj5g3f: the resolution takes entry [0] of a mixed-version list), two correct sessions will flip this file back and forth indefinitely, each with a truthful reason. The ping-pong is a symptom of -pj5g3f, not of anyone's carelessness, and it will keep costing blocked pushes until resolution is made deterministic. Do not read a future flip as an error by the session that made it.
